source.guideMeaning: Meals prepared at home; a useful natural compound.
source.sourceFidelity: The proposal retains the exact guide example as guide_original_example and labels its practice scenes as new situations; no source-question answer is asserted from the guide example.

sevenStepEditorialReview.reason: A uniquely identifies preparation in the family kitchen; B/C/D do not. The English then says they eat the packed lunch at school, making the entire family seem to attend school; Chinese repeats that implication. Name Jun as the person who packs/eats it.
A–D all plausibly explain where the packed lunch came from; B alone contains home-cooked food.

The prompt explicitly says the student cooked pasta at home. B says outdoors means it cannot be home-made and C says a lunch box proves restaurant origin. Both directly deny facts given, so the selection is trivial.
Restaurant takeaway eaten at home is not home-cooked; A/C are prepared at home.
A correctly distinguishes homely taste from preparation in a home kitchen. B/C represent common but overstated misconceptions; C could be made closer without changing the key.
Exact target span and bilingual distinction between cooking location and picnic location are correct.
A community dinner compares home-prepared soup with restaurant takeaway, changing the task from packed school lunch; two complete answers and five answer-derived glossary rows fit.

traditionalChinese: All question prompts, options, model sentences, writing answers and takeaways have intelligible Traditional Chinese with no decisive key or polarity mismatch. Any revised content needs a fresh bilingual check; rendered line wrapping has not been assessed.

existingOwnerComparison.relationship: Earlier owner is the whole sit down to a simple home-cooked dinner meal construction. This proposal isolates where the food was prepared, including food later eaten away from home; a distinct learner decision is supportable.

requiredFixes: Repair listening pronoun/coherence: Jun, not an unspecified whole family, packs and eats the food at school; update matching Chinese and regenerate that listening audio role if integrated.
Replace scene distractors with more credible near misses, such as food bought ready-made and reheated at home or food prepared at home but served elsewhere, while retaining one best answer.
Optional: make dialogue’s wrong options less absolute while still testing preparation versus familiar taste and eating place.
verdict: REVISE — scene distractors fail plausible-alternative gate; listening family/school referent also needs correction.
